19 During refuelling, a petrol car receives 50 litres of fuel in 90 seconds. The petrol has 34 MJ of
energy per litre.
For an electric car to receive the same amount of energy in the same time from a 230 V supply,
what is the minimum current required?
A
2700 A
B
8.2 × 104
A
C
7.4 × 106
A
D
6.6 × 108
A

hints: First find the total chemical energy delivered: $50$ litres multiplied by $34 \text{ MJ}$ per litre, then convert $\text{MJ}$ to $\text{J}$ using $1 \text{ MJ} = 10^{6} \text{ J}$.
That energy is delivered in $90 \text{ s}$, so the rate of energy transfer is $P = E/t$, and for the electric supply the same power must satisfy $P = VI$ with $V = 230 \text{ V}$.
Combine them as $I = E/(Vt)$ and watch the powers of ten: $10^{9} \text{ J}$ divided by $10^{2} \text{ V}$ and $10^{2} \text{ s}$ gives a current of order $10^{4} \text{ A}$.
walkthrough: Total petrol energy is volume times energy per litre: $E = 50 \times 34 \text{ MJ} = 1700 \text{ MJ}$.
Required power for delivery in $90 \text{ s}$ is $P = E/t = 1.7 \times 10^{9} / 90 \approx 1.89 \times 10^{7} \text{ W}$.
For the electric supply $P = VI$, so $I = P/V = E/(Vt)$.
Substitute with units: $I = 1.7 \times 10^{9} / (230 \times 90) \approx 8.2 \times 10^{4} \text{ A}$ with unit check $\text{J s}^{-1} \text{V}^{-1} = \text{A}$.

A.explanation: Gives a power of only about $0.62 \text{ MW}$, far less than the $≈19 \text{ MW}$ needed from 50 litres at $34 \text{ MJ}$ per litre in $90 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: Gives $P = VI \approx 1.9 \times 10^{7} \text{ W}$, which matches $E/t$ for $1.7 \times 10^{9} \text{ J}$ in $90 \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Equals $E/V$ without dividing by $90 \text{ s}$, so it is the total charge for the whole energy, not the current.

D.explanation: Equals $E \times t / V$, multiplying by $90 \text{ s}$ instead of dividing, so it is too large by a factor of $90^2$.
